answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique Minecraft server build history flips the bet — builds other players visited and rated — and the umber lands on the attacker instead. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because builds other players visited and rated is bound to a single identity — the raven is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the beacon of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
